top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) credits one mature body of work with transparent, re-runnable designs. The finding of large, persistent local adjustment costs from import competition has survived a decade of re-analysis, and the remaining debate concerns magnitudes and shift-share inference, not whether the effect exists. Autor and Dorn (2013) spans polarisation as well as the trade strand, so the citation, worded as empirical evidence on labour demand, polarisation and local adjustment, can be credited exactly to these three without claiming the task theory (Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu, Restrepo). I rank P002 (Autor, Hanson, Katz) second because it is a defensible variant if the committee defines the achievement as the broader wage-structure account, and its only difference from P001 is one name. I rank P003 (B014) third because its core is cleanly paired and mature, but the priority claims of Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum remain unresolved. I rank P004 (B045) fourth: it is a clean, mature methods contribution with narrower changed understanding and a Bresnahan attribution question. No award is last because every proposal on the slate rests on mature, well-confirmed work.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Katz, Helpman, Melitz, Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn. SSE colleagues Andersson, Friberg and Strömberg, and former committee member Johannesson as co-author, are disclosed ties that bear on no credited name.
